blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Hierarchical abstraction is a fundamental principle across many data modalities, enabling complex sequences to be represented compositionally at multiple levels. Learning such hierarchies directly from data, without explicit structural supervision, remains a central challenge in representation learning. We investigate whether meaningful hierarchical structure can emerge from compression alone. While autoencoders learn compressed representations through reconstruction, this objective does not necessarily favour meaningful compositional structure. We study this challenge through unsupervised grammar induction, where the underlying hierarchy can be evaluated explicitly. We introduce a hierarchical token-merging autoencoder that recursively combines adjacent tokens into increasingly abstract representations, compressing entire sequences through a variational information bottleneck. The model jointly learns representations and hierarchical structure by marginalising over possible binary trees using dynamic programming. To address training instability, we combine independently trained models through unsupervised consensus and distillation. Experiments on a synthetic, ambiguous grammar demonstrate the emergence of meaningful hierarchical structure without structural supervision. The resulting model achieves 93% grammatical parse-validity and 93% exact reconstruction on held-out sequences, compared with 42% parse-validity for the strongest trivial baseline. These findings establish a proof of concept for hierarchical token merging as a mechanism for unsupervised structure discovery and abstraction learning.
blocks.zh: 分级抽象是跨越许多数据模式的基本原则,使得复杂的序列能够在多层次上以组成方式得到体现. 直接从数据中学习这种等级制度,而没有明确的结构监督,仍然是代表性学习的一个中心挑战。 我们调查的是,仅从压缩中是否能够产生有意义的等级结构。 虽然自定义编码器通过重建来学习压缩表达,但这个目标并不一定有利于有意义的组成结构. 我们通过不受监督的语法诱导来研究这一挑战,在这种诱导中可以明确评价基本的等级。 我们引入了一种等级式的符号聚合自编码器,将相邻的符号递相地结合到越来越抽象的表示中,通过变异信息瓶颈来压缩整个序列. 该模型通过利用动态编程在可能的二进制树上边缘化来共同学习表现和分级结构. 为了解决培训不稳定的问题,我们通过不受监督的共识和提炼,将经过独立培训的模式结合起来。 关于合成,模棱两可的语法的实验表明,有意义的等级结构在没有结构监督的情况下出现. 由此产生的模型在被搁置序列上实现了93%的语法解析无效和93%的精确重建,而在最微小基线上则实现了42%的解析无效。 这些结论确立了一种概念的证明,即等级符号合并作为无监督的结构发现和抽象学习的机制.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Language is compositional, and so are many other kinds of sequence. Small units combine into larger ones hierarchically, and
those into larger ones again. Recovering that structure without annotation would be useful, because the
treebanks that supervised parsers rely on are expensive to build and specific to one language and domain, and
because whether grammatical structure can emerge with no supervision at all is a question of independent
scientific interest. The
question we study is whether a model can find constituent structure in raw token sequences, with no labelled
trees to learn from, with an information bottleneck as the only pressure towards structure.

This is hard for two reasons. First, a plain reconstruction objective is grammar-agnostic. An autoencoder that only
has to reproduce its input is rewarded for whatever structure is easiest to reconstruct, which may not be the
grammatical one. Second, the structure is a discrete object from a large space, since a sentence of n n tokens has
exponentially many binary trees; learning the representations and searching that space at the same time is
unstable. Models that induce latent trees often do well on their task without recovering structure that
matches human annotations ( Williams et al., 2018 ) , so reconstructing or predicting well is not the same as
parsing well.

This leads to our research question. Can a token-merging autoencoder induce grammatical structure from
raw tokens with no supervision, by scoring all possible trees at once, and if that induction works but is unstable, can
the instability be removed without reintroducing supervision?

blocks.en:
We make the following contributions. • We show that a token-merging autoencoder can induce grammatical structure from raw tokens with no
supervision, and from a deliberately minimal self-supervision (compression through a variational
bottleneck alone, with no outside pass and no reconstruction of words from their context), by
marginalising over trees rather than choosing a merge. In the best runs it recovers the grammar
with held-out parse-validity of 1.00. • We show that a single model is unreliable. Its induction is what we call a seed lottery. With
identical data and configuration, held-out parse-validity ranges from 0.01 to 1.00 depending only on the random
seed, and even the best-parsing models reconstruct
poorly, because the tight bottleneck that drives them to find structure also costs them the ability to
reproduce their input. • We find that combining many models at the level of individual constituents (span-based minimum Bayes
risk, span-MBR) beats combining whole trees, which matters on ambiguous data where good models disagree over equally
valid parses. Shayegh et al. (2024) use the same combination for ensembles of unsupervised parsers;
we show it remains effective when the members are runs of one model whose quality ranges from 0.01 to 1.00. • To make the method robust despite that lottery, we build a pipeline that trains many models, selects the
mutually consistent ones, combines them and distils the result into a single model that reaches a mean held-out
parse-validity of 0.93 and also reconstructs its input, which no single stage does alone. • We report a seven-pool robustness study, varying both the random seed and the data split, showing that
unsupervised selection mainly raises the weakest pools rather than improving every pool. • We find that, under the training schedules we tested, a single model does not reach both grammar and
reconstruction, because the two objectives compete for its capacity, so in our setting the two-stage separation
of induction from reconstruction is necessary rather than merely convenient. • We find that the two stages learn the grammar differently. The chart-trained base model, under the
compression bottleneck, organises its vocabulary by syntactic category as it discovers constituents, whereas
the distilled student reaches the same parse accuracy without clustering its word embeddings by category, so category structure is a
by-product of how structure is induced, not a prerequisite for parsing.

blocks.en: 2.1 Grammars, constituency and structure induction
blocks.zh: 2.1 语法、群体和结构简介

blocks.en:
Grammars describe how sequences decompose into nested constituents. A context-free grammar rewrites symbols
into strings of symbols, and a probabilistic context-free grammar (PCFG) attaches a probability to each rule,
so a sentence has a distribution over parse trees rather than one. The main difficulty for evaluation is ambiguity. A
single surface (token sequence) can have several valid parses, so a model may be right and still not match the one tree a
corpus happens to record. This shapes how we evaluate, and we come back to it in Section 4.1 . Unsupervised
induction of such grammars has a long history. The inside-outside algorithm estimates a PCFG by
expectation-maximisation ( Baker, 1979 ) ; the constituent-context model induces bracketings from the
distributions of spans and their contexts ( Klein and Manning, 2004 ) ; and neural and compound PCFGs parameterise the
rule probabilities with neural networks, which induces better grammars than classical PCFG estimation ( Kim et al., 2019 ; Yang et al., 2021 ) .
All of these learn an explicit symbolic grammar. Our model learns no rules. Structure is a by-product of
compressing the sequence, and there is no grammar to read off, only a tree per sentence.

blocks.en: 2.2 Marginalising over trees with CKY, the inside algorithm and Recursive Bayesian Networks
blocks.zh: 2.2 与 CKY 、 内在算法和递减性贝叶斯网络相比的树上边缘

blocks.en:
To score structure without choosing it we use a chart. The Cocke-Younger-Kasami recogniser fills a table
over spans and, for each span, combines the analyses of its sub-spans ( Younger, 1967 ) ; the inside
algorithm makes this probabilistic, summing over all derivations of a span in cubic time ( Baker, 1979 ) .
That sum is a differentiable function of the local scores, so a chart can be embedded in a neural model and be
trained by gradient descent. Recursive Bayesian Networks (RBNs) generalise the idea ( Lieck and Rohrmeier, 2021 ) . They
unify PCFGs, which have discrete symbols and tree structure, with dynamic Bayesian networks, which have
continuous latents and chain structure, and they extend inside and outside probabilities to continuous latent
variables. Our chart is an RBN inside pass whose latent at each span is a neural embedding. The framework also
suggests an explanation for the seed instability we report in Section 4.3 . Marginalising over
exponentially many structures turns the objective into a mixture with one component per structure, which is
non-convex, so gradient descent is not guaranteed to reach the global optimum, and optimising the
representations and the structure in turn (as expectation-maximisation does) is not the same as optimising them
together, as our model does. We interpret the seed dependence in Section 4.3 as a consequence of this
non-convexity.

blocks.en: 2.3 Neural latent-tree induction
blocks.zh: 2.3 神经潜在树木诱导

blocks.en:
The closest prior work is DIORA, an unsupervised inside-outside recursive autoencoder ( Drozdov et al., 2019 ) .
DIORA composes span representations with a soft, compatibility-weighted average on the inside pass, runs an
outside pass that reconstructs each word from its context, and reads a tree off the chart at test time. On the
full Wall Street Journal corpus it reaches an unlabelled constituency F1 of 55.7 on average against a
right-branching baseline of 16.5, and it varies little across seeds (about ± 0.5 \pm 0.5 F1). Our chart differs
from it in four ways. It is inside-only, so we drop the outside pass. It aggregates a span with a hard
straight-through choice instead of a soft blend, so a span is one analysis and not a mixture of all of them. It
reconstructs the whole sentence from a single root vector through a variational bottleneck, instead of
predicting each word from its local context, so it has an explicit information bottleneck where DIORA has none.
And its objective, which must reconstruct the whole sentence from a single bottlenecked vector, is not
seed-stable where DIORA is; the ensemble and distillation stages of our method are designed to compensate for
that instability ( Section 4.3 ). Other neural models induce a latent tree jointly with a downstream
objective ( Yogatama et al., 2017 ; Choi et al., 2018 ; Havrylov et al., 2019 ) , and syntax-aware sequence
models bias recurrent networks toward hierarchy without an explicit chart ( Shen et al., 2018 ; Shen et al., 2019 ) . Williams et al. (2018) show that latent-tree learners can do well on their end task while the trees they
induce do not match meaningful structure. Accordingly, our evaluation
reports grammatical validity rather than claiming linguistic correctness.

blocks.en: 2.4 Structured autoencoders and discrete latent variables

blocks.en:
Our model combines several standard components. Recursive autoencoders learn representations of tree nodes by
encoding and decoding their children ( Socher et al., 2011b ) , and the recursive neural network that first built
trees for scenes and language did so by greedily merging the adjacent pair with the best composition score ( Socher et al., 2011a ) . We keep the recursive merge of adjacent pairs but replace the greedy score with
marginalisation over all trees. The bottleneck is a variational autoencoder ( Kingma and Welling, 2014 ) ; its β \beta -weighted form sets the weight of the penalty on the latent’s divergence from its prior, and hence how
much information the latent retains ( Higgins et al., 2017 ) ; we rely on this penalty to favour structured
encodings. To keep the merge a hard decision while still training by gradient descent
we use continuous relaxations of discrete variables, the Gumbel-softmax or Concrete distribution ( Jang et al., 2017 ; Maddison et al., 2017 ) , with the straight-through estimator that passes a hard sample
forward and a soft gradient backward ( Bengio et al., 2013 ) . We reuse these components unchanged. What
is new is not any one of them but their combination, a chart-based merge autoencoder in which a compression
bottleneck, rather than any label, is what drives the structure.

blocks.en:
The name token merging also appears in a different literature, where tokens are merged to reduce the
computational cost of transformers, not to recover structure. Spectrum-preserving merging ( Tran et al., 2024 ) and
agglomerative token clustering ( Haurum et al., 2024 ) are recent examples, and one method,

blocks.en: 2.6 Consensus decoding and distillation
blocks.zh: 2.6 共识解码和分解

blocks.en:
The ensemble stage of our method builds on two ideas. Minimum Bayes risk decoding returns not the single
highest-scoring structure but the one that minimises expected loss under a distribution over structures; for
trees that means maximising the expected number of correct constituents ( Goodman, 1996 ) , which is why combining candidate
parses span by span behaves differently from voting over whole trees. A span-level combination can return a
tree that no single model proposed, whereas a whole-tree vote cannot. Ensembling independent models reduces
variance, and knowledge distillation compresses an ensemble into one model ( Hinton et al., 2015 ) . We use
both, with one difference. Our ensemble is a set of independently seeded parsers combined once, offline, into a
single set of silver trees (machine-produced trees used as training targets in place of gold annotations), not
an ensemble queried at test time.

The closest prior work on this side of the method is Shayegh et al. (2024) , who combine an ensemble of

from failing to perfect, and we choose which members to keep without supervision.

blocks.en: 2.7 Summary and gap

blocks.en:
In our work we build a token-merging autoencoder that induces structure from a compression bottleneck alone,
together with a CKY inside pass that lets it score every tree instead of choosing one. This induction
succeeds in some runs but varies strongly across seeds, so a single model is a seed lottery. To turn that into one reliable parser we combine
many models and distil the result into one, an approach also taken by Shayegh et al. (2024) . The rest of the paper describes the method and reports both what it does and
where it is fragile.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: 3.1 Overview
blocks.zh: 3.1 概览

blocks.en:
The task is to recover the constituent structure of a sentence without being shown any structure during
training. We work with sentences of between two and eight tokens drawn from a small probabilistic grammar in
which many sentences have more than one valid parse. Bounding the length keeps the number of possible binary
trees small enough to enumerate exhaustively at evaluation time. Section 4.1 describes the data in full.
blocks.zh:
任务是恢复某一句子的构成结构,而不在其中显示任何结构
培训。 我们从一个小概率语法中 得出两到八个符号
许多句子有多个有效的解析。 绑定长度保留可能的二进制数
树木小到可以在评价时详尽列举。 第4.1节全面描述了数据。

blocks.en:
The pipeline uses a single architecture for two different jobs. That architecture, which we call the base
model, is a variational autoencoder built from four networks, a lifter, a merger, an unmerger and an
unlifter. Figure 1 shows how the three stages fit together.
blocks.zh:
管线采用单一架构,用于两个不同的工作. 我们称之为基地的建筑
模型,是一种由四个网络、一个起重机、一个合并、一个不合并和一个
无取者. 图1显示三个阶段如何融合。

blocks.en:
In the first stage we train N N independently initialised base models and freeze each one when training ends.
Its learning rate decays to near zero by step 2,500, after which its weights are fixed ( Section 3.3.4 ).
Every base model learns to compress a sentence into a single vector by repeatedly merging adjacent pairs,
choosing the merge order for itself. Trained with a tight bottleneck (a Kullback–Leibler (KL) weight of β = 0.04 \beta=0.04 , Table 2 ), these models become good parsers but
poor reconstructors. They recover the grammar while losing the ability to reproduce the input tokens. Their
quality also varies sharply between runs, even though every model sees identical data and differs only in its
random initialisation and the order in which it receives the training examples. That variability is why we
train many models rather than one ( Section 4.3 ).

培训许多模式而不是一种模式(第4.3节)。

another while failed models disagree in idiosyncratic ways. The retained models then vote on individual
constituents rather than on whole trees, and a dynamic program assembles the best-supported constituents into
one tree per sentence. The result is a single silver treebank.

blocks.en: 3.2 The token-merging autoencoder
blocks.zh: 3.2 国家 自动编码器

blocks.en:
We designed the base model as a recursive β \beta -VAE whose decoder is guided by the tree along which the
encoder has merged. The model has four neural networks, a lifter, a merger, an unmerger and an unlifter. The
lifter maps tokens into the embedding space. We then apply a single merger recursively, first to the leaf
tokens and then to the intermediate constituent representations it produces, and this is the encoder.
Similarly we apply a single unmerger recursively to the root latent, and this is the decoder. The
unlifter maps the recovered latents to a distribution over the vocabulary, from which the output tokens are
predicted.
blocks.zh:
我们设计了一种折叠性β\β-VAE的基模,其解码器由树导出。
编码器已经合并 。 该模型有四个神经网络,一个起重机,一个合并,一个不合并和一个不升起. 这个
升起器将符号映射入嵌入空间. 然后我们递相实施一次合并 首先在叶子上
符号,然后是它的中间组成代表, 这是编码器。
同样,我们把单一的不合并递归到根基中,这是解码器。 这个
解析器将回收的潜伏物映射到词汇表上的分布,输出符号就是从这些词汇表上的
预言。

blocks.en:
While training the base models we score all trees with the chart ( Section 3.3 ) rather than committing to a
single one, so every split of every span receives a gradient, rather than only the splits of one chosen tree. We kept the
base model deliberately simple, so that we could test whether the architecture induces grammar at all rather
than to maximise capacity; a small model also makes ablations easier to interpret.
blocks.zh:
在训练基本模型时,我们用图表(第3.3节)对所有树木进行评分,而不是承诺
单一,因此每个跨度的每一个分出都会得到一个梯度,而不是只得到一个所选树的分出. 我们留着
基础模型故意简单, 以便我们可以测试 建筑是否诱导语法
而不是最大限度地提高能力;一个小的模型也更容易解释。

blocks.en: 3.2.1 The four networks
blocks.zh: 3.2.1 国家 四个网络

blocks.en:
The lifter maps each token to a latent and is stochastic, with two embedding tables giving a mean and a
log-variance and the latent sampled by the reparameterisation trick, so a word is a distribution rather than a
point. The merger is the encoder step, a small multilayer perceptron that takes a left and a right latent and
outputs the mean and log-variance of their parent, a latent with the same dimension and prior as a leaf latent, so one merger runs at
any depth of the tree. The unmerger is the decoder step, a deterministic network trained to approximately invert the
merger, mapping a parent back to a predicted left and right child. The squared error between its predictions and the actual
children measures how invertible a merge is, and this same quantity scores the candidate splits in the chart
( Section 3.3 ). The unlifter is a single linear layer from a latent to scores over the vocabulary, kept
deliberately weak so the model cannot use a powerful decoder to compensate for a poorly chosen structure. The
full architecture is shown in Appendix A .

点。 合并是编码器步骤,一个小的多层感应器,它取出左和右两侧的潜入.

blocks.en: 3.2.2 Bottleneck and training on a fixed tree
blocks.zh: 3.2.2 固定树上的博特伦克和培训

blocks.en:
The forward pass on a given tree has two parts. We first map every token to a latent with the lifter, then
apply the merger bottom-up along the tree until a single root latent remains. Decoding works back down the
same tree through the unmerger, and finally the unlifter turns each recovered leaf latent into a distribution
over the vocabulary.

沿着树上应用自下而上合并,直到一个单一的根潜在残留。 解码工作回到下面
同一棵树通过未合并, 最后不升起器 将每个恢复的叶子 潜入分布
超越词汇。

blocks.en:
The decoder starts from the root latent alone and is given none of the encoder’s intermediate latents. This
forces the model to compress, and our assumption is that the lowest-cost way to encode a sentence in one vector
is to merge it along its grammatical constituents. If we carried the encoder’s
intermediate latents across, the model could reconstruct without compressing and there would be no pressure to
find structure.

迫使模型压缩, 我们的假设是,最低成本的方法 编码句子在一个矢量
将它与语法成分合并 如果我们携带编码器
中间潜伏物跨越,模型可以在不压缩的情况下重建,不会有压力。
寻找结构。

We regularise both leaf latents and merged latents toward the same N ⁡ ( 0 , I ) N(0,I) prior. We chose a shared prior so

at any level; in the objective below this KL is weighted by β \beta .

blocks.en: 3.3.2 Straight-through aggregation

blocks.en:
Two different quantities are involved here, and only one of them is soft. The span score is a soft
sum, the log-sum-exp over splits of Equation 2 , which is what keeps the objective
differentiable. The representation passed up from a span, however, must be a single vector, so for it
we select one split with a hard Gumbel sample on the forward pass while letting the gradient flow through the
soft weights. This is the straight-through estimator. The score is therefore soft while the chosen merge stays a
genuine discrete decision. The Gumbel temperature is annealed from 2.0 to 0.5 over 10,000 steps; since the
base models train for only 2,500 steps, the temperature only falls from 2.0 to about 1.63 during their training,
the high, exploratory part of that schedule. We accumulate only the selected split’s KL, since the same
hard weights choose both the representation and its KL. Two alternatives are available, a plain argmax and a soft blend over the candidate splits. We compare all three and justify this choice in Experiment 1.

blocks.en: 3.4 From many parsers to one treebank
blocks.zh: 3.4 国家 从许多解析器到一棵树

blocks.en:
We train many base models as parsers, because even with the same training set their quality varies. Because we
want to keep the method unsupervised, we cannot score them all against gold trees and keep the best; instead we select
the best ones without supervision and then combine their parses. To select, we rank the models by their mean
agreement with every other model, where the agreement of two models is the fraction of training sentences on
which their parse trees are identical (peer agreement), and keep the third with the highest peer agreement. We use
this because we assume that bad models fail in mutually disagreeing ways while good models converge on similar,
correct parses, so agreement is a usable proxy for quality. To combine, each selected model votes for the
constituents in its parse of each sentence, and we build the silver tree from the bracketing with the most
total span support, where the support of a span is the number of selected models whose tree contains it, which is minimum Bayes risk decoding at the level of constituents ( Goodman, 1996 ) . We work at the level of
constituents rather than whole trees because, on ambiguous data, two good models may produce different but
equally valid trees; a whole-tree vote would split their support and could discard a good model, whereas a
constituent-level vote lets partially agreeing models reinforce the spans they share ( Section 4.4 ). Finally,
we use agreement only to select the models and then let them vote uniformly, since agreement already decides which models are
retained, and weighting by it as well would further favour the models closest to the majority, whether or not
the majority is correct.

blocks.en: 3.5 Distillation into a single model
blocks.zh: 3.5 蒸馏成单一型号

blocks.en:
The consensus gives us a silver treebank, one tree for every training sentence. We train a fresh student model
on it with our fixed-tree objective ( Equation 1 ), teacher-forced on the silver trees, that is, trained with each silver tree given as the merge order. We distil a
student because the base models are good parsers but poor reconstructors, a consequence of the tight bottleneck
that forces them to find structure. Fixing the structure first lets the student devote its capacity to
reconstruction rather than on discovering how to bracket a sentence. The two stages therefore act as a
curriculum. A tight bottleneck in the first stage induces the grammar at the cost of reconstruction, and a
looser bottleneck in the second stage learns to reconstruct on the now-fixed trees. Grammar discovery and
reconstruction are separated in time rather than traded off inside one model, using the same architecture
under different objectives at the two stages. Whether one model could instead do both on its own, by training
longer or loosening its bottleneck rather than separating the stages, is tested directly in Experiment 6. The student
is given a larger latent (embedding dimension 48), a
smaller KL weight ( β = 0.002 \beta=0.002 ) and a longer schedule (12,000 steps) than the base models. The
reconstruction this recovers is reported in Experiment 4, and the sweep of the student’s KL weight that places
this value on the reconstruction-favouring end of the trade-off in Experiment 5.

blocks.en: 4.1 Setup
blocks.zh: 4.1 设置

blocks.en:
Our grammar is a small ambiguous probabilistic grammar in the style of English, with 19 terminal words in six
categories (subjects, verbs, gradable adverbs, non-gradable adverbs, grade modifiers and verb qualifiers)
and 7 non-terminals. Its ambiguity comes from recursive rules. A grade may modify a grade, and a verb may take
qualifiers and adverbs, so many surfaces have several distinct valid parses. 63.1% of surfaces admit more
than one, and the average surface admits 4.34. Ambiguity grows sharply with length. Sentences of length two
and three are unambiguous, while at length eight 94.8% of surfaces are ambiguous and the average admits 10.8
parses. Sentences are of length 2 to 8, sampled by
derivation, so each comes with the gold tree that generated it. A single surface can occur as several
sentences, one for each distinct derivation the grammar assigns it, so the number of sentences exceeds the
number of distinct surfaces. We split by surface, holding out 10% of the distinct surfaces at each length;
this gives 1370 distinct surfaces in total, which yield 1510 training and 174 held-out sentences.

We evaluate the distilled model with three metrics. Parse-validity is the fraction of held-out sentences whose
predicted tree is a valid parse under the grammar (the baselines in Table 1 are averaged over
surfaces instead). Recon-exact is the fraction whose tokens, decoded from the
single root vector along the tree with the lowest ℒ tree \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{tree}} , are recovered exactly. Gold-match is the fraction whose predicted tree equals the
sentence’s gold tree. Parse-validity is our primary metric, because our aim is to recover any valid analysis
rather than one particular tree; gold-match is deliberately stricter, since under ambiguity the model can pick
a different but valid parse, and it tells us how often it recovers the exact sampled tree. Gold trees are used
only in evaluation, never in training, selection, or the consensus.

ambiguous grammar F1 against a single gold tree is a lower bound rather than a measure of correctness, since a

structure as the target, which is what parse-validity measures.

length cap. Finally, the chart runs on the latent means rather than on samples ( Section 3.3 ); only the
student, which trains on fixed trees, samples its latents.

blocks.en:
Setup. On each of the seven pools we combined the eight selected models both ways, span-based minimum
Bayes risk, which the pipeline uses, and a whole-tree majority vote, and scored the resulting silver treebank
against the grammar on the training surfaces. We also distilled a student on each silver treebank in turn, with
training otherwise identical, to test whether the choice affects the distilled student.

贝叶斯冒险,管道使用, 和整棵树多数票, 得分 由此产生的银树银行
与训练表面的语法相对. 我们还依次在每个银树上分泌了一个学生
培训在其他方面是相同的,以测试选择是否影响到被蒸馏的学生。

blocks.en:
Results. Span-MBR matches or beats the vote in all seven
pools, raising the mean consensus from 0.867 to 0.933, with a worst case of an exact tie rather than a
regression. The gain concentrates where the whole-tree vote is weakest. In pool 52–75 the vote returns only
0.616 even though the pool contains a model with parse-validity 1.000 on the training surfaces, and combining at the constituent level lifts that
pool to 0.887. The whole-tree vote never beats its own best member in any of the seven pools. The advantage
carries over to the distilled student, as the span-MBR student matches or beats the whole-tree-vote student on held-out
validity in all seven pools, by 0.068 on average and by 0.287 in pool 52–75.

agree on the constituents but disagree over which equally valid whole tree to report, so their support is

where good models often return different but equally valid trees, the combiner must therefore work on
constituents; otherwise the student inherits the lower-quality treebank. This is consistent with Shayegh et al. (2024) , who combine

Discussion. The random-draw sweep shows the variance reduction expected of an ensemble. The two sweeps diverge because they do different things. Adding a random model adds diversity, whereas
adding a peer-ranked model adds a model the ranking has already judged worse than everything above it, so once
the highest-ranked models are included, each further model tends to lower the consensus. That peer agreement predicts gold-scored validity so well means an
unsupervised quantity we can compute is a reliable stand-in for the supervised one we cannot. We therefore
retain eight models. Eight is not the value with the best average, since retaining two is marginally better on
the mean, but it is the value with the best worst case, and we prioritise the worst pool over the mean because the purpose of the
pipeline is a reliable result from any pool. Retaining two gives up 0.048 in the worst pool to gain 0.018 on average. The choice is also
insensitive; across the range from six to twelve models the average moves by only 0.012, so eight sits on a
plateau rather than at a spike, which matters because the value was chosen with knowledge of these gold-scored
results rather than on a separate development set ( Section 4.8 ). 3 3 3 The figure for two models should not be read as evidence that a
two-model ensemble combines well. With two models the combiner almost always returns the better of the two
rather than anything new. Across the seven pools its mean advantage over the better member is + 0.0008 +0.0008 , and
in one pool the consensus reproduces the better model’s tree on all 549 sentences where the two disagree. That
column measures how good a model the selection rule can find, not what combining achieves.

blocks.en: 4.5 Experiment 4, the main result across seven independent pools

blocks.en:
Setup. We ran seven independent pools of 24 base models each ( Table 5 ). Four vary only the random
seed on a single data split and so measure initialisation and optimisation variance. The other three vary the
data split as well. Our sampler is reseeded for each, so these are fresh draws of sentences from the same
grammar rather than re-partitions of the same corpus, and the four distinct splits give held-out sets of 174,
171, 165 and 172 sentences. Together they separate the two sources of variability the result might have
been sensitive to.

数据也分开。 我们的采样器被重新播种, 所以这些是新鲜的句子 从相同的
语法而不是重新分出 同一体, 四个不同的分裂 给予搁置 174套,
171,165和172个句子. 它们共同将结果可能存在的两种变异源分离出来
被敏感的。

blocks.en:
Results. Student results are similar under both sources of variation. Distilled students reach 0.839 to 0.989 across seeds and 0.855 to 0.994 across
splits, and the two groups have almost the same mean. The pipeline reduces the 0.01 to 1.00 spread of single
base models to 0.839 to 0.994, and redrawing the data does not widen it.

blocks.en:
The students also reconstruct far better than the base models they are distilled from. Across the four seed-varying pools the
median base model recovers its input exactly on only 0.147 to 0.198 of held-out sentences, and the worst on
0.023, whereas the students reach 0.925 to 0.971. This roughly fivefold gain comes from fixing the structure
before learning to reconstruct, which is the point of training a second model with a looser bottleneck (Experiment 6 tests a
single-model alternative).

0.023,学生达到0.925至0.971. 这大概是五倍的收益 来自于修复结构
在学习重建之前,这是培训第二个具有更宽松瓶颈的模型的要点(经验6测试a)

Selection does not improve every pool; its benefit is concentrated in the weakest pools. Three pools are
already strong without it, and on those it lowers the result, by up to 0.10 (pool 100–123 falls from 0.969 to
0.867). It raises the weakest pools instead. The worst pool, 52–75, improves from 0.630 to 0.887 and split 1 from 0.805 to 1.000, and across all seven the mean rises
from 0.886 to 0.933 while the minimum rises from 0.630 to 0.844. Peer-agreement selection therefore raises the worst case
rather than improving every pool, at a cost on pools that are already strong.

blocks.en:
One limitation bounds what the ensemble can claim. The consensus never
beats the best individual model in its pool, unlike the ensembles of different parsers in Shayegh et al. (2024) . Pools 52–75 and 124–147 each contained a model with parse-validity
1.000 on the training surfaces, and the consensus matched neither. What the consensus does is reliably approach the validity of a good model
without knowing which model that is, and that is the appropriate comparison. Against the best model
identifiable without gold trees (the one our own selection rule ranks first), consensus wins over the four
seed-varying pools on training surfaces, 0.92 against 0.80 on average and by much more in the worst case,
0.867 against 0.555. The consensus therefore acts as a
variance-reduction step rather than a source of gains beyond the best member. Because parse quality cannot be
measured without gold trees, the best model in a pool cannot be identified at training time; the ensemble
recovers near-best performance reliably from a pool whose individual outcomes are, by the seed lottery,
unpredictable.

A final check tests whether the distilled model has learned the grammar or merely memorised the silver trees
it was trained on. The split is by surface, so no held-out sentence appears in training, but the student could
in principle still overfit the training brackets. The evidence is against memorisation. On the two pools
examined this way, 52–75 and 76–99, parse-validity on training surfaces (0.900 and 0.980) matches held-out validity (0.868 and
0.989) to within sampling noise, so there is no generalisation gap. The student reproduces the silver trees it
was given on 0.905 and 0.995 of training surfaces, so it is a faithful distillation whose grammar transfers to
unseen surfaces rather than a memorisation of the training trees.

blocks.en:
Discussion. Across all seven pools, gold-match averages 0.494 while validity averages 0.927. This gap is
expected under ambiguity rather than a shortfall in the grammar the model has learned. 63.1% of surfaces admit
more than one valid parse, and at length eight the average surface has about eleven of them, so a model that has
learned the grammar will frequently return a valid tree other than the one our sampler happened to draw.
Moreover, an ambiguous surface appears once per sampled derivation, each with its own gold tree, so a single
predicted tree can match at most one of them. The same gap appears in unlabelled bracketing F1, the standard parsing metric, computed across all
seven pools. F1 against the sampled gold tree averages 0.78 (range 0.74 to 0.81), but against the best-matching
valid parse it averages 0.98 (range 0.95 to 1.00). The model recovers almost every constituent of some valid
analysis, and the shortfall against gold is a choice among valid parses, not an error (these figures are for
our enumerable grammar and are not comparable to F1 on natural corpora). Table 6 breaks the
students down by length and shows where the remaining errors sit. In two of the three pools validity is at least
0.92 at every length and 1.000 up to length five, and all three degrade at seven and eight,
exactly where the number of competing analyses grows fastest, from 3.5 per surface at length six to 5.8 at
seven and 10.8 at eight.

blocks.en: 4.6 Experiment 5, what the latent space represents
blocks.zh: 4.6 实验5,潜在空间代表什么

blocks.en:
Figure 5: Cosine similarity between the nineteen word embeddings, ordered by category, for the best base
model (held-out parse-validity 1.000) and the distilled student (0.989). The base model groups words by
category; the student does not, yet both parse well. A sweep of the student’s KL weight (holding latent
size fixed) does not reproduce the clustering, so it is a by-product of how the base models induce
structure, not of the bottleneck and not a prerequisite for parsing.

型号(持有-出解-活性1.000)和蒸馏生(0.989)。 基本模式组合词组
类别; 学生没有, 两者都很好。 浏览学生的KL体重( 持有潜伏)
大小固定)不复制集群,因此它是基模型如何诱导的副产品.
结构,不是瓶颈,也不是解析的先决条件。

blocks.en:
Setup. The best base model and the distilled student learn the grammar equally well, their held-out
parse-validity being 1.000 and 0.989 respectively, but they represent the vocabulary differently. We compare
them through the cosine similarity between the nineteen word embeddings of each, ordered by category
( Figure 5 ).
blocks.zh:
设相. 最好的基模 和蒸馏的学生 学习同样好的语法, 他们坚持
解析效力分别为1 000和0.989,但它们代表的词汇不同。 我们比较
它们通过每一个嵌入的十九个单词的同位素相似性,按类别排序
(图5)

blocks.en:
Results. The best base model groups words tightly by syntactic type. Sixteen of the nineteen words
have a same-category nearest neighbour, and verbs, grade modifiers and gradable adverbs each form a distinct
block. The student shows little such grouping. Only seven of its nineteen words have a same-category nearest
neighbour, and for verbs, grade modifiers and gradable adverbs, none of the three words in each category has a
same-category nearest neighbour; its word vectors have pairwise cosine similarities close to zero.
blocks.zh:
结果。 最佳的基底模型按综合类型严格地组合词. 十九个字中的十六个
近邻有同一类,动词、等级修饰和可分级副词各形成一个不同的
块。 学生很少表现出这样的群体。 其十九个字中只有七个字有同一类最接近
相邻者,对于动词,等级修饰和可分级的副词,每类三个词中没有一个有:
同类近邻;其单词矢量有近于0的对等余弦相似性.

blocks.en:
Discussion. That a model can parse as well as the base model with little grouping of words by category tells us the
student’s grammar is not carried by where its word vectors sit. The structure is in which vectors are
merged, not in their arrangement in the space. The natural explanation for the difference would be the
bottleneck, since the base models compress far harder than the student, but a controlled sweep argues
against it. Holding the latent size fixed and raising the student’s KL weight from 0.002 to 0.05, past the base
models’ 0.04, reconstruction degrades as expected, from 0.95 to 0.86, while category cohesion (the fraction of words whose nearest neighbour is in the same category) does not
increase, and at every setting the student groups words far less than the base model does. The base
models’ word-category structure is therefore a property of how they are trained (they must induce the
grammar by scoring every tree, where the student receives its trees from the consensus) rather than of compression
pressure, though we do not isolate the cause further. The
network that performs the induction, with no category labels and no gold trees, organises the vocabulary by
syntactic type, which is consistent with chart-marginalised training recovering the grammar’s categories and
not only its brackets. Whatever its cause, word-category geometry is a by-product of structure induction, not a prerequisite for parsing, and the
student parses without it.

学生的语法不是由其单词“向量”所在位置所承载的。 结构是矢量所在
合并,不在空间安排中 区别的自然解释是

在每次设置时,学生团体的言词都远远低于基准模式。 基础
因此,模型的词类结构是其培训方式的属性(它们必须诱导
语法通过评分每棵树, 学生从共识得到树) 而不是压缩
尽管我们没有进一步孤立原因, 这个
执行入门的网络,没有分类标签和金树,组织词汇
综合类型,与图边化培训相一致,恢复语法类别和
不仅是它的括号。 无论原因如何,词类几何是结构诱导的副产品,而不是解析的先决条件,以及
学生们没有它,就自责。

blocks.en: 4.7 Experiment 6, a single model trained longer does not replace the two stages
blocks.zh: 4.7 试验6, 训练时间更长的单一模型不能取代两个阶段

blocks.en:
Setup. The pipeline separates structure induction from reconstruction across two models, a tight base
model and a looser student trained on fixed trees. A natural question is whether one model
could do both if it were trained for longer, removing the need for a second stage. We tested this on
four seeds that individually induce the grammar, whose base models reach held-out parse-validity between 0.90
and 1.00 and whose reconstruction is low as the tight bottleneck requires, near 0.13. For each seed we ran three
15,000-step strategies, all of which share the base model’s tight first 2500 steps and then differ in how
training continues. The first restarts the learning rate at its maximum and keeps the bottleneck tight. The
second uses the same restart but drops the KL weight to the student’s 0.002. The third uses no restart at all,
a single smooth learning-rate decay with the bottleneck held tight, which is equivalent to training the base model
for longer. The frozen base model is the reference. The three questions are whether more training recovers
reconstruction, whether the restart is needed, and whether loosening the bottleneck helps.
blocks.zh:
设相. 管道将结构诱导与重建分开,跨越两个模式,一个紧凑的基地
模特儿和一个在固定树上训练的松散学生 一个自然的问题 是一个模型
如果培训时间更长,就能够做到两者兼而有之,从而不再需要第二阶段。 我们试了这个
4个种子分别诱发语法,其基本模式在0.90之间被搁置
和1.00, 重建低于紧要的瓶颈需要, 接近0.13。 每个种子,我们跑三
15,000分步战略,它们都分享了基础模型紧凑的前2500分步,然后在如何
培训仍在继续。 第一种会以最大的速度重启学习率,并保持瓶颈的收紧. 这个
II 使用相同的重启,但将 KL 重量降低到学生的0. 02. 第三个完全不用重启,
单平滑的学习率衰减 与瓶颈紧紧地保持, 这相当于培训基础模型
更长时间。 被冻结的基座模型就是参考. 三个问题是 更多的培训是否恢复
重建, 是否需要重新启动, 以及解开瓶颈是否有帮助 。

blocks.en:
Results. More training recovers reconstruction in every strategy ( Table 7 ), from
about 0.13 at the base model to between 0.61 and 0.85, but it plateaus there by around 12,000 steps and never
reaches the distilled student’s
0.93. Loosening the bottleneck does not help. The loose arm is no better than the tight one on either metric, a
median change of − 0.011 -0.011 in validity and − 0.060 -0.060 in reconstruction. The restart is not needed and can be
harmful. The no-restart arm matches the restart on grammar across the four seeds, a median difference of 0.000 0.000 in validity, and it rescues seed 93, whose validity the learning-rate restart reduced from 1.000 to 0.328;
without the restart its validity is 0.799, at a reconstruction cost of 0.13 (0.718 against 0.851). Seed 93 also shows
the trade-off inside a single model most clearly. When its grammar collapses under the restart, to validity
0.328, reconstruction rises to the run’s highest value, 0.851, whereas the no-restart run that keeps the
grammar at 0.799 reconstructs less, at 0.718.
blocks.zh:
结果。 每项战略(表7)中,更多的培训恢复了重建(表7)。
在基座模型上大约0.13到0.61到0.85之间,但是它在那里高地上约12,000个台阶,从不
到达蒸馏学生

blocks.en:
Discussion. A single model reconstructs worse than the student not because its bottleneck is too
tight, since loosening it did not help, but because it must still induce structure while it reconstructs, and
the two objectives share its capacity. Seed 93 makes this visible, with reconstruction highest exactly where
validity has fallen. The student avoids the trade-off because it is trained on fixed trees and devotes all
of its capacity to reconstruction, which is why it reaches 0.93. Training one model for longer removes neither
the reconstruction plateau (0.61 to 0.85) nor the seed lottery, since these runs begin from seeds that already induce the grammar and still
spread, seed 93 ending between 0.33 and 0.80 depending only on the learning-rate schedule. The pipeline
provides the two properties the single model lacks, reliability from combining many seeded models and reconstruction
quality from a student trained on fixed trees. This is the two-stage separation of structure induction from
reconstruction, a frozen parser supplying the trees and a fresh model learning to reconstruct on them, and the
experiment shows that it is the separation, not a schedule inside one model, that lets the final model reach
both. We tested four seeds that induce the grammar and three schedules, so the claim is about this ceiling and
this lottery rather than a proof that no single-model schedule could ever do better.

blocks.en: 4.8 Limitations and future work
blocks.zh: 4.8 限制和今后的工作

blocks.en: Several factors limit what these results support; we quantify two of them.
blocks.zh: 有几个因素限制了这些成果的支持;我们量化其中两个。

blocks.en:
The first concerns variance across pools. Our results are a distribution over pools rather than a
point estimate, and our original four pools shared a single data split, so they measured only initialisation
variance. The three additional pools in Table 5 redraw the data, and the distilled students
span 0.855 to 0.994 across splits against 0.839 to 0.989 across seeds. Data variance is therefore no larger
than seed variance. Seven pools remains a small sample, and all seven come from one grammar.

blocks.en:
The second is selection. The pipeline is unsupervised in the sense that no gold tree influences any model it
produces, but the rule for how many models to retain was chosen while we could see gold-scored results, which
is a form of tuning on the test set. We tried to remove that dependence by calibrating the rule on a separate,
unambiguous development grammar and transferring it unchanged, and it did not transfer. Over the four seed-varying
pools, the transferred rule averages 0.876 against 0.923 for the rule we use, and 0.796 against 0.867 in the worst case, because on an
unambiguous grammar validity means recovering the single correct tree, one of 429 at length eight, whereas on
our ambiguous grammar it means recovering any of roughly eleven, so the two grammars do not ask the same
question. We therefore quantify the dependence rather than leave it implicit. The selection rule is chosen with
knowledge of these pools, and closing that gap by fixing the rule without gold-scored feedback would cost
approximately 0.05 on average and 0.07 in the worst case. Every model the pipeline produces is still
unsupervised; the residual dependence is confined to this one scalar.

The remaining limitations are not quantified. Our metrics are not produced by identical procedures, since base
models are scored using the chart’s own parse whereas the student’s parse comes from enumerating every tree and
taking the one with the lowest ℒ tree \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{tree}} ( Equation 1 ). The scale is small (19 words, sentences of length 2 to 8, a held-out set of 174
sentences), and exhaustive enumeration is tractable only under that bound, which is also what makes the
evaluation possible in the form we use. Validity is not correctness ( Williams et al., 2018 ) . A tree can be
grammatical without being the analysis a linguist would choose, and the gold-match figure of 0.494 should be
read alongside the validity figure of 0.927. Because the student is distilled from the consensus, it can be
no better than the silver trees that supervise it, so any consistent but wrong bracketing the consensus settles
on is inherited by the student, and parse-validity, which accepts any valid tree, cannot detect it.

blocks.en:
Finally, and most importantly, every result here is on a synthetic
grammar, and we make no claim about natural text. A grammar of nineteen words with six categories and a bounded
sentence length is a controlled setting chosen so that exhaustive enumeration, exact ambiguity counts and
exact random-tree baselines are all available. Those same properties are what natural corpora lack, which
is precisely why we begin here. The scope of the present contribution is that setting. We establish that
compression alone induces grammar, that the induction is a seed lottery, and that ensembling and distillation
convert the lottery into a single reliable parser. Extending this to natural text is the next step, and Section 5 sets out the concrete obstacles (the loss of exhaustive enumeration and exact baselines chief among
them) that such an extension must address.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We asked whether a token-merging autoencoder can induce grammatical structure from raw tokens with no
supervision, by scoring all trees rather than choosing a merge, and whether that induction, if unstable, can be
stabilised without supervision. The answer to the first question is positive. The architecture recovers the grammar, in the best
runs with held-out parse-validity of 1.00, from a compression objective alone. The answer to the second is positive in aggregate. A
single model is a seed lottery, so we train many, keep the ones whose parses agree most often with the others’, combine their parses span by span,
and distil the result into one model. That model reaches a mean of 0.93 parse-validity and 0.93 reconstruction on
held-out sentences, against a parse-validity of 0.42 for the strongest trivial baseline (right-branching), and it holds up across seven pools that
vary both the random seed and the data itself, with no gold trees used anywhere but evaluation.

Three further findings follow. First, unsupervised selection by peer agreement raises the worst case
rather than improving every pool. It raised our worst pool, from 0.63 to 0.89, and cost a strong one 0.10, raising the

rather than from how many are combined. Agreement among models predicts their gold-scored accuracy well, so adding
models the selector has already ranked low makes the consensus worse, even though adding models at random
makes it better. Third, the consensus never exceeds the best model in its pool; its benefit is a higher worst case, not gains
beyond the best member. It approaches the validity of a good model without knowing which model that is, and
against the best model we can identify without gold trees it wins in the worst case by 0.31 (0.867 against
0.555).

These results come from a small synthetic grammar and rest on a configuration chosen partly with knowledge of
results. Section 4.8 sets out these limitations in full, including our unsuccessful attempt to remove the
dependence of the retention rule on gold-scored results.

blocks.en:
Several directions follow. The selection rule still needs a way of being fixed without reference to the
evaluation data. Our attempt to calibrate it on a development grammar failed because validity means something
different on an unambiguous grammar than on an ambiguous one, so a transferable criterion would have to be
defined on a quantity that does not change meaning with the grammar. The next step is natural text,
which we have not attempted here and which will need an approximate chart, since exhaustive enumeration is
tractable only at short lengths; the same bound is what makes our evaluation exact, so moving to natural text
sacrifices exact evaluation. A more direct approach is a syntax-aligned objective (a context or cloze term in the manner of the
inside-outside autoencoder, or a neural grammar parameterisation), which would address the seed variance of
single models directly.
Our ensemble exists because single models are unreliable, and the results above suggest the ensemble can only
ever be as good as the best model it contains. Making that model reliable would be worth more than any
improvement to how they are combined.
